payload.title: DIP-B02: Evaluate worktree-aware scope coordination and merge-aware handoffs
payload.description: The longitudinal controlled experiment observed actual shared-file ownership refusals across isolated worktrees (7 captured hook denial records and 10 denied MCP claim replies). All 4 DIP projects still encountered a pipeline.mjs merge conflict, as did all 4 controls. Workers deliberately forked the same base and were committed only after both finished; waiting could not update the other worker's branch in this schedule. Final quality remained identical (120/120 primary, 52/52 exact intent, 9216/9216 exploratory stress per arm). This is a local scheduling/merge-handoff limitation to investigate, not evidence that all scope locking is ineffective or that conflicts imply lost code.
acceptance: Profile actual contention, waiting and repeated model/tool loops using the published raw traces before changing scope policy.
Evaluate how to allow legitimate edits in isolated worktrees while preserving same-worktree fencing and ownership of the same logical task; make branch/base freshness visible.
Test merge-aware handoffs under induced overlap and report code preservation, coordination cost and remaining Git conflicts without promising automatic conflict-free integration.
